Given $tanA + 3cosB + 6sinC = 1;$ $3tanA + cosB + 4sinC = 4$ and $5tanA + 3cosB - 8sinC = - 2 .$

Let $P = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & 3 & - 8\end{cases}\right], X = \left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right]$ and $Q = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 4 \\ - 2\end{array}\right] .$

Then, the system of equations can be written as $PX = Q .$

Hence, we have $X = {P}^{- 1}Q .$

Now $\left|P\right| = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & 3 & - 8\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|P\right| = 1\left(- 8 - 12\right) - 3\left(- 24 - 20\right) + 6\left(9 - 5\right)$

$⇒ \left|P\right| = - 20 + 132 + 24 = 136 .$

The cofactors of the elements of the matrix $P$ are

${A}_{11} = - 8 - 12 = - 20, {A}_{12} = - \left(- 24 - 20\right) = 44, {A}_{13} = 9 - 5 = 4,$

${A}_{21} = - \left(- 24 - 18\right) = 42, {A}_{22} = - 8 - 30 = - 38, {A}_{23} = - \left(3 - 15\right) = 12,$

${A}_{31} = 12 - 6 = 6, {A}_{32} = - \left(4 - 18\right) = 14, {A}_{33} = 1 - 9 = - 8 .$Thus, the adjoint matrix of $P$ is

$adjP = \left[\begin{cases}- 20 & 42 & 6 \\ 44 & - 38 & 14 \\ 4 & 12 & - 8\end{cases}\right] .$

And ${P}^{- 1} = \dfrac{adjP}{\left|P\right|},$

$⇒ {P}^{- 1} = \dfrac{1}{136}\left[\begin{cases}- 20 & 42 & 6 \\ 44 & - 38 & 14 \\ 4 & 12 & - 8\end{cases}\right] .$

The solution of the given system is

$\left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \dfrac{1}{136}\left[\begin{cases}- 20 & 42 & 6 \\ 44 & - 38 & 14 \\ 4 & 12 & - 8\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 4 \\ - 2\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \dfrac{1}{136}\left[\begin{array}{ll}- 20 \times 1 + 42 \times 4 + 6 \times \left(- 2\right) \\ 44 \times 1 + \left(- 38\right) \times 4 + 14 \times \left(- 2\right) \\ 4 \times 1 + 12 \times 4 + \left(- 8\right) \times \left(- 2\right)\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \dfrac{1}{136}\left[\begin{array}{ll}136 \\ 136 \\ 68\end{array}\right]$

$⇒ x = tanA = 1, y = cosB = - 1$ and $z = sinC = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

Also, $A$ and $C$ lie in $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $B$ lies in $\left[0, 2\pi\right] .$

Thus $tanA = 1, ⇒ A = \dfrac{\pi}{4}, cosB = - 1, ⇒ B = \pi$ and $sinC = \dfrac{1}{2}, C = \dfrac{\pi}{6} .$

Now $B - 2A - C = \pi - 2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} .$
